newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Amoco, Agip set up firm to operate gas field.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Amoco, Agip set up firm to operate gas field.

text.p: Egypt's state oil corporation, Amoco Corp and the Egyptian affiliate of Agip SpA have set up a company to operate four gas-producing concessions off the Nile Delta, industry sources said on Monday.
The company, to be known as Mediterranean Gas, will operate in the Baltim, Timsah, Ras el-Barr and East Delta Deep concessions, all of which are shared by Amoco and Agip.
The state's Egyptian General Petroleum Corp (EGPC) has 50 percent of the new company and the other 50 percent is split evenly between the foreign companies, they said.
Once an Egyptian concession produces oil or gas, it is normal procedure for EGPC and the foreign concession holder to set up an operating company in 50-50 partnership.
"To their credit, EGPC realised it would be inefficient to do this for each of the four concessions so we will have one operating company for all four," a company executive said.
The company will be operating what oil executives are describing as a "world-class gas basin". Egypt has plans to export the gas to Turkey, Jordan, Israel and Lebanon.

The chairman of the new company is Hani Hafez, formerly chairman and managing director of Suez Oil (SUCO), a similar operating company joint venture between EGPC, Deminex of Germany and Repsol of Spain.
